key_insight: E-RLBM independently relaxes nonhydrodynamic modes, continuously bridging BGK and regularized collision operators without changing Navier–Stokes viscosity.
engineering_relevance: A low-cost, two-rate collision operator can enlarge the stable simulation domain without requiring a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.
method: Project nonequilibrium distributions onto the second-order hydrodynamic Hermite sector.
Apply a separate relaxation time to the complete complementary kinetic subspace.
Use Chapman–Enskog and linear shear analysis to characterize viscosity and higher-order errors.
evidence_signal: Taylor–Green vortex and obstacle-flow tests show improved stability; all three operators achieve second-order Taylor–Green convergence, with E-RLBM error about 6% above BGK and 40% below RLBM.
watch_item: Kinetic relaxation changes direction-dependent fourth-order shear errors, so stability gains require attention to accuracy and parameter selection.
